environment.description: Same Terraform provider backend on EC2 in account 998877665544 under OU ou-r4nd-prodinfra. MongoDB 6.0 with SCRAM-SHA-256 auth enabled (readOnly user for provider). IAM role arn:aws:iam::998877665544:role/TerraformProviderExec has permission boundary arn:aws:iam::998877665544:policy/PB-InfraReadOnly attached which explicitly denies dynamodb:*, s3:Delete*, and all iam:* actions. Account is subject to SCP arn:aws:organizations::112233445566:policy/p-svc9x2m1 which contains a Deny statement for 'Effect:Deny, Action:[mongodb-internal:AdminCommand, ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute], Resource:*' with condition 'StringNotEquals aws:PrincipalOrgID o-abc123def'. The MongoDB user 'tf_provider_ro' has only the 'read' built-in role on database 'terraform_state' — no write, no delete, no admin privileges. Network path restricted via prefix list pl-0a1b2c3d4e (only /32 of the ALB internal IPs). Note: the permission boundary and SCP do not directly interact with MongoDB wire protocol; the actual gate is the MongoDB RBAC role assignment limiting the authenticated session to find() operations only, which prevents the DeleteMany exploit path and limits NoSQL injection impact to read-only data exfiltration within the single authorized database.
